{{Short description|Paradox of deontic logic created by James William Forrester}}
{{Orphan|date=December 2021}}

'''Forrester's paradox''', also known as the '''paradox of gentle murder''', is a [[paradox]] of [[deontic logic]] attributed to [[James Forrester (philosopher)|James Forrester]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Sinnott-Armstrong|first=Walter|date=1959|title=A solution to Forrester's paradox of gentle murder|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.5840/jphil195956233|journal=Journal of Philosophy|volume=56|issue=2|pages=162–168|doi=10.5840/jphil195956233|issn=0022-362X|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Goble|first=Lou|date=1991|title=Murder Most Gentle: The Paradox Deepens|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/4320256|journal=Philosophical Studies|volume=64|issue=2|pages=217–227|doi=10.1007/BF00404830|jstor=4320256|s2cid=170715161|issn=0031-8116|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Meyer|first=J.-J.Ch.|date=1987|title=A simple solution to the "deepest" paradox in deontic logic|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/44084186|journal=Logique et Analyse|volume=30|issue=117/118|pages=81–90|jstor=44084186|issn=0024-5836}}</ref> It is a version of the [[Good Samaritan paradox]].

Forrester's argument is that, starting from the statements that:
* it is obligatory (under the law) that Smith not murder Jones, and
* it is obligatory that, if Smith murders Jones, Smith murder Jones gently,
it logically follows that:
* if Smith murders Jones, it is obligatory, that Smith murder Jones gently.
However, if it were actually the case that Smith murdered Jones, it can then be deduced that:
* it is obligatory, that Smith murder Jones,
which contradicts the first statement, leading to a [[logical fallacy]].<ref name=Forrester1984>{{Cite journal|last=Forrester|first=James William|date=1984|title=Gentle Murder, or the Adverbial Samaritan|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2026120|journal=The Journal of Philosophy|volume=81|issue=4|pages=193–197|doi=10.2307/2026120|jstor=2026120|issn=0022-362X|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

A number of arguments have been advanced that Forrester's paradox is invalid, for example that it is the result of a confusion of scope,<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Clark|first=Romane|date=1986-08-01|title=Murderers are not obliged to murder; another solution to Forrester's paradox|url=https://doi.org/10.1080/05568648609506248|journal=Philosophical Papers|volume=15|issue=1|pages=51–57|doi=10.1080/05568648609506248|issn=0556-8641|url-access=subscription}}</ref> or a misuse of deduction rules.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Peterson|first1=Clayton|last2=Marquis|first2=Jean-Pierre|date=2012-10-01|title=A Note on Forrester's Paradox|url=https://www.pdcnet.org/pdc/bvdb.nsf/purchase?openform&fp=pjphil&id=pjphil_2012_0006_0002_0053_0070|journal=Polish Journal of Philosophy|language=en|volume=6|issue=2|pages=53–70|doi=10.5840/pjphil20126213|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
